FOCUSED.name: FOCUSED
FOCUSED.purpose: Deconstructing messy problem spaces into ruthlessly scoped MVPs

steps.name: Find the problem
steps.desc: What is the core structural pain point rather than the noisy symptom?

steps.name: Outline user segments
steps.desc: Who experiences this friction and what are their distinct incentives?

steps.name: Crystallize the pain
steps.desc: Quantify the real cost of inertia in time, capital, or compliance risk.

steps.name: Understand alternatives
steps.desc: How is the problem solved today and where do existing workarounds break?

steps.name: Scope the solution
steps.desc: Define crisp MVP boundaries that validate the riskiest assumption.

steps.name: Execute MVP
steps.desc: Build the simplest automated workflow that delivers tangible value.

steps.name: Define metrics
steps.desc: Establish leading North Star metrics and counter-metric guardrails.

workedExample.problem: ESG compliance officers at Indian NBFCs spend 3+ weeks compiling BRSR reports manually

applied.F: Compliance officers at mid-sized NBFCs waste 15–20 days per reporting cycle collecting, verifying, and formatting non-standardized ESG data across disparate branch offices.
applied.O: Primary: ESG Compliance Officers at NBFCs (500–5,000 employees). Secondary: Chief Financial Officers who sign off disclosures. Tertiary: Board Audit Committees.
applied.C: At ₹1.5L/month avg salary × 0.75 months wasted = ₹1.12L per officer per reporting cycle. 500 NBFCs × 2 officers = ₹11.25 Cr industry productivity loss.
applied.U: Disjointed Excel sheets (60%), high-priced Big 4 advisory (30%), monolithic legacy enterprise suites (10% — too complex/costly for mid-market).
applied.S: MVP Scope: Automated ingestion of utility bills + diesel generator logs → auto-calculate Scope 1 & 2 GHG emissions → pre-fill SEBI BRSR Principle 6 table. Single principle, single entity.
applied.E: Upload-based web tool with OCR parsing, emission factor lookup table, and instant PDF/Excel export. Piloted with 5 mid-tier NBFCs.
applied.D: North Star: Time-to-complete BRSR Principle 6 drops from 5 business days to under 4 hours. Guardrail: 0% calculation discrepancies against standard GHG Protocol factors.

GAME.name: GAME
GAME.purpose: Structured bottom-up and top-down estimation under incomplete information

steps.name: Ground the question
steps.desc: Define the exact boundary conditions, geography, and unit of measurement.

steps.name: Assumptions & anchors
steps.desc: Anchor against verified reference facts and regulatory mandates.

steps.name: Math layer by layer
steps.desc: Construct transparent formulas with clear multipliers and conversion rates.

steps.name: Error-check & sanity
steps.desc: Stress-test the result against macro industry revenues and sanity bounds.

workedExample.problem: How many ESG software buyers exist in India in 2026?

applied.G: Estimating the total number of enterprise and mid-market organizations in India actively purchasing automated ESG accounting software in FY26.
applied.A: SEBI BRSR mandate covers top 1,000 listed entities. RBI draft norms impact ~85 major NBFCs & urban cooperative banks. ~50 public sector undertakings and ~500 voluntary mid-corps with global supply chain commitments.
applied.M: 1. Mandated listed (top 1,000) × 70% unserved by modern SaaS = 700 entities. 2. Regulated BFSI (135 entities) × 60% procurement intent = 81 entities. 3. Voluntary exporters (500 entities) × 30% conversion = 150 entities. Total Addressable Active Buyers = 931 organizations.
applied.E: At an average annual contract value of $25,000 (₹21 Lakhs), 931 buyers represent an addressable domestic SaaS ARR of ~$23.3 Million (₹195 Cr), matching industry analyst estimates of India's ESG SaaS expansion.

SIFTED.name: SIFTED
SIFTED.purpose: Rigorous estimation of multi-tiered environmental & operational variables

steps.name: Scope it
steps.desc: Fix boundary, timeline, and precise carbon/cost metric.

steps.name: Identify segments
steps.desc: Partition universe into mutually exclusive, collectively exhaustive buckets.

steps.name: Fact-anchor each segment
steps.desc: Attach empirical data points to each bucket.

steps.name: Think through conversion
steps.desc: Apply carbon emission factors and operational multipliers.

steps.name: Estimate range
steps.desc: Provide confidence intervals (P10, P50, P90) rather than point estimates.

steps.name: Defend your logic
steps.desc: Identify key sensitivity levers and what conditions break the model.

workedExample.problem: Estimate daily carbon emissions from food delivery fleets in Mumbai

applied.S: Total daily CO₂e emitted by last-mile motorized meal deliveries across the Mumbai metropolitan region in 2026.
applied.I: Fleet Segments: ICE 2-wheelers (petrol) ~85%, Electric 2-wheelers (EV) ~12%, Non-motorized bicycles ~3%.
applied.F: Total daily deliveries in Mumbai: ~1,200,000 orders. Average trip distance (restaurant to doorstep + idle leg): 4.8 km.
applied.T: ICE Bikes: (1.02M trips × 4.8 km) × 58g CO₂/km = 284 tonnes. EV Fleet: (144K trips × 4.8 km) × 18g CO₂/km (grid avg) = 12.4 tonnes. Bicycles: 36K trips × 0g = 0 tonnes. Mid Estimate: ~296.4 tCO₂e/day.
applied.E: P10 (Low): 240 tCO₂e (higher EV cluster adoption). P50 (Expected): 296 tCO₂e. P90 (High): 365 tCO₂e (monsoon detour and high idle-traffic factors).
applied.D: Sensitivity analysis: Fleet electrification is the primary lever. A 20% shift from ICE to EV reduces fleet emissions by 53 tonnes CO₂ daily.
